metadata.title: IP102 to Terrace Gardening Pest Knowledge Base Mapping

mappings.rationale: Obligate monophagous/oligophagous pest of paddy rice fields; not found in urban container terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Lepidopteran leaf rolling symptom superficially resembles tortricid moth damage on ornamentals, but biological host is strictly graminaceous.

mappings.rationale: Wetland paddy rice defoliator; unrecorded on rooftop container garden flora.
mappings.known_limitations: General noctuid larval morphology can resemble vegetable cutworms, but ecological niche is restricted to flooded paddy.

mappings.rationale: Dipteran stem borer specialized on paddy rice stems and panicles.
mappings.known_limitations: Damage symptoms (deadheart) resemble other stem borers but host range excludes terrace garden vegetables.

mappings.rationale: Major economic stem borer of flooded agricultural rice fields.
mappings.known_limitations: Larval stage feeds internally in cereal culms; not applicable to terrace container plants.

mappings.rationale: Monophagous pest strictly dependent on lowland paddy rice ecosystems.
mappings.known_limitations: Whiteheads and deadhearts are specific to gramineous panicles.

mappings.rationale: Cecidomyiid gall midge creating 'silver shoot' galls exclusively in rice culms.
mappings.known_limitations: No cross-infestation to rooftop container plants.

mappings.rationale: Ephydrid shore fly attacking flooded rice leaves in standing water.
mappings.known_limitations: Requires standing aquatic paddy conditions to reproduce.

mappings.rationale: Major migratory delphacid hopper of wetland paddy causing hopperburn in floodplains.
mappings.known_limitations: Delphacid hopper morphology is distinct from terrace garden cicadellids; host is strictly rice.

mappings.rationale: Graminaceous wetland hopper restricted to rice and wild paddy grasses.
mappings.known_limitations: Does not colonize dicotyledonous terrace garden crops.

mappings.rationale: Vector of rice stripe virus in cereal monocultures; irrelevant to terrace container gardening.
mappings.known_limitations: Small planthopper feeding restricted to Poaceae.

mappings.rationale: Aquatic curculionid weevil whose larvae feed on submerged rice roots in aquatic fields.
mappings.known_limitations: Adults feed on rice leaf blades; larvae require saturated anaerobic submerged mud.

mappings.rationale: Green rice leafhopper primarily infesting rice fields and transmitting tungro/dwarf viruses.
mappings.known_limitations: While a cicadellid, its ecological niche and host specificity are rice-bound.

mappings.rationale: Predominantly a spikelet and glume feeder on cereal crops (wheat, rye, rice); not validated for terrace vegetables.
mappings.known_limitations: Phlaeothripid morphology differs significantly from common terrace Thripidae (Frankliniella/Scirtothrips).

mappings.rationale: Spiny beetle (rice hispa) mining and scraping leaves exclusively in paddy monocultures.
mappings.known_limitations: Leaf-mining beetle specific to rice foliage.

mappings.rationale: White grubs occasionally occur in container potting mixes containing uncomposted farmyard manure, chewing container rootlets.
mappings.known_limitations: Subterranean root feeder rarely visible in canopy foliage photographs; foliar beetle treatments are inappropriate.

mappings.rationale: Deep burrowing subterranean insect found in native pasture and field soils, absent from elevated rooftop potting mix containers.
mappings.known_limitations: Foliar imagery cannot diagnose soil-tunneling orthopterans.

mappings.rationale: Click beetle larvae feeding in open agricultural soil on tuber crops; absent from containerized terrace potting media.
mappings.known_limitations: Underground pest not identifiable on foliage.

mappings.rationale: Crambid moth uncommon in urban environments; insufficient evidence of terrace vegetable crop damage.
mappings.known_limitations: Adult moth morphology often confused with other crambids.

mappings.rationale: Cosmopolitan pest that severs young terrace container seedlings (tomato, pepper, brinjal, beans) at soil level at night.
mappings.known_limitations: Larvae hide under container mulch by day; foliar detection relies on severed stems or direct nocturnal sightings.

mappings.rationale: Polyphagous noctuid cutworm that attacks container herbs and vegetables during cool seasons.
mappings.known_limitations: Visual appearance overlaps closely with other noctuid larvae.

mappings.rationale: Defoliator of solanaceous and brassica crops in terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Commonly a variant naming for Spodoptera instars.

mappings.rationale: Two-spotted spider mite / red spider is one of the top destructive pests on urban terrace container gardens during hot dry spells.
mappings.known_limitations: Extremely small body size (0.5 mm) means photographs often capture webbing and stippling rather than sharp individual mite anatomy.

mappings.rationale: Occasionally attacks container sweet corn on terrace gardens, boring into ears and stalks.
mappings.known_limitations: Infrequent on typical vegetable-focused terrace gardens unless sweet corn is specifically cultivated.

mappings.rationale: Voracious foliage feeder attacking container crops in marching swarms when nearby lawns or grassy weeds are mowed.
mappings.known_limitations: Severe defoliation overlaps with multiple Lepidopteran species.

mappings.rationale: Ubiquitous primary pest of containerized terrace garden crops (tomatoes, chillies, eggplants, beans, greens, roses).
mappings.known_limitations: Forms dense colonies; visual patterns include shed white exuviae skins, honeydew droplets, and secondary sooty mold.

mappings.rationale: Flower chafer beetle whose adults occasionally feed on terrace fruit tree blossoms and overripe fruits.
mappings.known_limitations: Generally an incidental flower visitor rather than a primary container garden destroyer.

mappings.rationale: Clearwing moth borer attacking trunks of commercial orchard stone-fruit trees; unrecorded on terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Requires mature woody trunks of Prunus species.

mappings.rationale: Cereal aphid species capable of feeding on ornamental grasses and small container grain experiments.
mappings.known_limitations: Rarely infests standard terrace solanaceous or cucurbitaceous crops.

mappings.rationale: Greenbug aphid attacking grasses, sorghums, and small grain containers on terraces.
mappings.known_limitations: Narrower host preference than polyphagous Myzus persicae.

mappings.rationale: Cereal aphid that migrates between bird cherry trees and grasses.
mappings.known_limitations: Non-target on container terrace vegetables.

mappings.rationale: Dipteran midge attacking wheat florets in broad-acre fields; absent from terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Monophagous on developing cereal heads.

mappings.rationale: Red-legged earth mite; feeds on container peas, beans, and winter greens causing silvering.
mappings.known_limitations: Active primarily during cold damp winter months; distinct black body with red legs.

mappings.rationale: Brown wheat mite / longlegged mite feeding on leaves of container monocots and legumes.
mappings.known_limitations: Lacks heavy silken webbing typical of Tetranychus urticae.

mappings.rationale: Phlaeothripid thrips infesting cereal ears; limited terrace vegetable relevance.
mappings.known_limitations: Darker and larger than foliage thrips.

mappings.rationale: Stem-mining sawfly of broad-acre wheat fields.
mappings.known_limitations: Strictly cereal stem pest.

mappings.rationale: Agromyzid leafminer attacking grasses and container leeks/chives.
mappings.known_limitations: Less prevalent on terrace gardens than polyphagous Liriomyza species.

mappings.rationale: Mangold/beet fly whose larvae mine large blister-like blotches in container spinach, chard, and beetroot leaves.
mappings.known_limitations: Produces blotch mines rather than thin serpentine mines.

mappings.rationale: Extremely prevalent on terrace container eggplants, brassicas, radishes, and tomatoes, riddling leaves with circular shot-holes.
mappings.known_limitations: Small jumping beetles that rapidly scatter when approached.

mappings.rationale: Major pest of container cabbage, cauliflower, kale, and broccoli on terrace gardens, devouring leaves and boring into heads.
mappings.known_limitations: Foliar damage can look identical to other brassica caterpillars.

mappings.rationale: Common container garden pest attacking tomatoes, peppers, spinach, peas, and ornamentals.
mappings.known_limitations: Young instars skeletonize leaves in groups before dispersing as solitary chewers.

mappings.rationale: Anthomyiid leafminer attacking containerized Chenopodiaceae foliage.
mappings.known_limitations: Creates translucent blister mines on beet greens.

mappings.rationale: Web-spinning caterpillar feeding on container vegetables in outbreak seasons.
mappings.known_limitations: Sporadic migratory occurrences.

mappings.rationale: Broad-acre sugar beet pest; occasionally chews seedlings of containerized beets and chard.
mappings.known_limitations: Primary economic impact is in commercial beet farming.

mappings.rationale: Nocturnal leaf-chewing chafer beetle attacking terrace container fruit foliage and ornamentals at night.
mappings.known_limitations: Adults feed nocturnally, making daytime photographic detection difficult.

mappings.rationale: Curculionid weevil whose larvae skeletonize container legumes, clover, and peas.
mappings.known_limitations: Prefers forage legumes over fruiting vegetables.

mappings.rationale: Flax crop specialist confined to commercial oilseed regions; irrelevant to urban terrace gardening.
mappings.known_limitations: No host plants in standard container terrace gardens.

mappings.rationale: Mirid plant bug (Miridae) feeding on flower buds and shoots. True bug (Heteroptera), not a leafhopper (Cicadellidae).
mappings.known_limitations: Causes blossom drop and shoot distortion; biologically distinct from leafhoppers.

mappings.rationale: Polyphagous mirid plant bug (Miridae, Heteroptera) feeding on flowers, fruits, and apical meristems. Downgraded from validated because it is a true bug, not a leafhopper (Cicadellidae).
mappings.known_limitations: Mobile true bug; symptoms include cat-facing and apical necrosis. Cannot be treated as a cicadellid leafhopper.

mappings.rationale: Chewing defoliator (Orthoptera); incidental visitor chewing container leaves, biologically distinct from sap-sucking hoppers.
mappings.known_limitations: Chewing defoliator; does not cause hopperburn or vector viral pathogens.

mappings.rationale: Blister beetle (Meloidae) feeding on flowers. Contains cantharidin toxin; unmapped from beetle_weevil to prevent unsafe bare-hand picking advice.
mappings.known_limitations: Cantharidin causes chemical burns and blisters; requires protective equipment if handled.

mappings.rationale: Blister beetle (Meloidae) devouring flowers. Contains cantharidin toxin; unmapped from beetle_weevil to prevent unsafe bare-hand picking advice.
mappings.known_limitations: Vesicant beetle; bare-hand removal is hazardous to skin.

mappings.rationale: Blister beetle family (Meloidae). Unmapped from beetle_weevil to avoid generic handpicking recommendations that could induce dermatosis.
mappings.known_limitations: Cantharidin blister toxin present in hemolymph.

mappings.rationale: Spotted alfalfa aphid feeding on container forage legumes, secreting copious honeydew.
mappings.known_limitations: Distinct dark spots on abdominal dorsum.

mappings.rationale: Thrips species feeding on legume blossoms (lotus, clover, peas).
mappings.known_limitations: Infestation restricted to papilionaceous flowers.

mappings.rationale: Major global pest of containerized chillies, capsicums, tomatoes, and roses on terrace gardens, causing boat-shaped upward leaf curling and silvering.
mappings.known_limitations: Minute slender insects often concealed inside flower buds and curled young leaves.

mappings.rationale: Tiny seed-infesting wasp specialized on commercial alfalfa seed pods; irrelevant to terrace gardening.
mappings.known_limitations: Attacks only developing seed within pods.

mappings.rationale: Indian cabbage white butterfly whose green caterpillars severely defoliate terrace container cabbage, cauliflower, radish, and kale.
mappings.known_limitations: Cryptic green coloration blends seamlessly into crucifer leaf veins.

mappings.rationale: Green plant bug (Miridae) feeding on tender growing tips and flower buds. Heteroptera, not a leafhopper.
mappings.known_limitations: Causes necrotic puncture spots on foliage and shoot tip withering.

mappings.rationale: Stinging slug caterpillars feeding on leaves of containerized fruit trees (mango, guava, pomegranate, citrus) on terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Equipped with urticating stinging spines that cause severe dermal irritation upon contact.

mappings.rationale: Specialist gall aphid of commercial grape rootstocks; rarely relevant to urban container terrace plants.
mappings.known_limitations: Forms root and leaf galls on specific Vitis varieties.

mappings.rationale: Grape erineum mite (Eriophyidae). Microscopic gall mite causing blister-like white erineum felts, not a web-spinning spider mite.
mappings.known_limitations: Microscopic eriophyid mite causing erineum patches rather than webs.

mappings.rationale: Citrus flat mite / false spider mite infesting container citrus, pomegranates, and ornamentals on terraces.
mappings.known_limitations: Flat red body, does not spin heavy webbing.

mappings.rationale: Ten-spotted grape leaf beetle defoliating container grapevines and related vitaceae.
mappings.known_limitations: Host-restricted to grapevines.

mappings.rationale: Broad mite is a major pest of chilli/pepper ('murda' downward leaf curling). Downgraded from validated: belongs to Tarsonemidae, not Tetranychidae (spider mites). Does not spin webs; standard spider mite advice is misleading.
mappings.known_limitations: Microscopic tarsonemid mite (0.2 mm); diagnostic certainty requires detecting downward leaf curling without webbing.

mappings.rationale: Comstock mealybug infesting stem crevices, node joints, and flower calyxes of containerized fruit trees and ornamentals on terraces.
mappings.known_limitations: Covered in heavy white mealy wax; excretes copious honeydew attracting ants.

mappings.rationale: Sesiid clearwing moth borer attacking woody forest/oak trees.
mappings.known_limitations: Wood borer of commercial timber, not garden container plants.

mappings.rationale: Sphingid hawkmoth caterpillar feeding on container grapevines on rooftop terraces.
mappings.known_limitations: Large horned caterpillar consuming substantial foliage rapidly.

mappings.rationale: Spotted lanternfly; invasive fulgorid planthopper swarming on container grapevines and fruit trees.
mappings.known_limitations: Quarantine pest in multiple regions; distinct polka-dot wings and red hindwings.

mappings.rationale: Cerambycid longhorn wood-boring beetle attacking thick tree trunks; absent from terrace container gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Internal borer of large mature tree wood.

mappings.rationale: Green leafhopper causing stippling, marginal yellowing, and hopperburn on container vegetables and ornamental plants.
mappings.known_limitations: Active hopper that leaps away when foliage is disturbed.

mappings.rationale: Family of sap-sucking plant bugs (Heteroptera). True bugs, not leafhoppers (Cicadellidae, Auchenorrhyncha).
mappings.known_limitations: Diverse family containing both herbivorous pests and predatory beneficials.

mappings.rationale: Greenhouse whitefly is a premier terrace gardening insect pest globally, attacking tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, eggplants, and herbs.
mappings.known_limitations: Adults flutter up in white clouds; nymphs are flat translucent waxy scales on leaf undersides.

mappings.rationale: Grape leafhopper feeding on foliage of container grapevines and fruit plants, causing pale stippling.
mappings.known_limitations: Specific to woody perennial climbers.

mappings.rationale: Asian swallowtail butterfly larva regularly found defoliating container lemon, lime, and citrus trees on urban terraces.
mappings.known_limitations: Early instars resemble bird droppings; late instars are large smooth green caterpillars with osmeteria horns.

mappings.rationale: Citrus red mite is a rampant pest of potted terrace citrus trees (lemon, calamondin, kumquat), turning dark green leaves into dusty silvery chlorotic foliage.
mappings.known_limitations: Dark red globular mites with distinct white bristles arising from tubercles.

mappings.rationale: Citrus rust mite (Eriophyidae). Microscopic rust mite causing rind russeting and bronzing; not a web-spinning spider mite (Tetranychidae).
mappings.known_limitations: Microscopic wedge-shaped eriophyid mite undetectable without magnification.

mappings.rationale: Cottony cushion scale attacking container citrus, roses, and woody terrace shrubs, producing large fluted white egg sacs.
mappings.known_limitations: Morphologically transitional between scales and mealybugs; fluted ovisac is distinctive.

mappings.rationale: Arrowhead scale; armored scale requiring specific orchard-scale chemical/biological regimes not represented in PEST_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.
mappings.known_limitations: Diaspidid armored scale; distinct from soft mealybugs.

mappings.rationale: Red wax scale encrusting perennial branches; distinct wax-capped scale not in standard terrace pest protocols.
mappings.known_limitations: Coccid scale with hard pinkish-red waxy dome.

mappings.rationale: Florida red scale; hard armored scale attacking leaves of container citrus and palms.
mappings.known_limitations: Armored scale requiring oil sprays; not directly mapped to soft mealybug protocol.

mappings.rationale: Black parlatoria scale; black rectangular armored scale of citrus.
mappings.known_limitations: Strictly armored scale.

mappings.rationale: Spherical mealybug / hibiscus mealybug is one of the most aggressive terrace pests, infesting container hibiscus, citrus, tomato, and eggplant stems.
mappings.known_limitations: Forms globular clusters covered in dirty-white or yellowish sticky wax.

mappings.rationale: Orange spiny whitefly; nymphs are spiny black scales fringed with white wax on citrus leaf undersides.
mappings.known_limitations: Appearance is black and spiny, unlike the powdery white adults of Trialeurodes.

mappings.rationale: Chinese citrus fruit fly; orchard-level tephritid pest ovipositing in developing citrus.
mappings.known_limitations: Larval damage is internal fruit decay; adult fly is rarely photographed stationary on leaves.

mappings.rationale: Oriental fruit fly; causes maggot infestation in terrace container tomatoes, guavas, and peppers.
mappings.known_limitations: Tephritid fruit borer; requires pheromone traps rather than contact foliar sprays.

mappings.rationale: Japanese orange fly specialized on commercial mandarin orchards.
mappings.known_limitations: Orchard-restricted tephritid.

mappings.rationale: Asian tobacco cutworm / cluster caterpillar is a devastating polyphagous pest on container tomatoes, chillies, eggplants, beans, and leafy greens on terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Egg masses are covered in pale hair scales; larvae exhibit dramatic color polymorphism.

mappings.rationale: Obscure regional tree gall maker not found on urban terrace gardens.
mappings.known_limitations: Taxonomic rarity in home gardening contexts.

mappings.rationale: Citrus leafminer is practically guaranteed to attack new leaf flushes on potted terrace lemon, lime, and citrus trees, carving distinctive silvery serpentine mines.
mappings.known_limitations: Larva stays strictly inside leaf parenchyma until pupating at rolled leaf edge.

mappings.rationale: Brown citrus aphid infests tender shoot flushes of containerized citrus trees on terraces, curling young leaves and vectoring citrus tristeza virus.
mappings.known_limitations: Colonies are deep brown to shiny black, clustering on stem tips.

mappings.rationale: Black citrus aphid infesting container citrus, camellia, and flowering terrace shrubs.
mappings.known_limitations: Audible stridulation under intense disturbance; black clustered colonies.

mappings.rationale: Spirea aphid / green citrus aphid heavily infesting terrace container citrus, apple saplings, and ornamentals.
mappings.known_limitations: Bright yellowish-green to green bodies clustering on terminal buds.

mappings.rationale: Chilli thrips / yellow tea thrips is the single most common cause of severe leaf curling and stunted growth in container terrace chillies and roses.
mappings.known_limitations: Extremely minute (less than 1 mm); symptoms appear as brown rasping along veins and boat-shaped upward cup.

mappings.rationale: Gall midge causing leaf rolling galls on specific host trees or alfalfa.
mappings.known_limitations: Cecidomyiid requiring specialized identification.

mappings.rationale: Flatid planthopper whose nymphs coat branches in powdery white waxy filaments.
mappings.known_limitations: Wax filaments easily mistaken for mealybug colonies.

mappings.rationale: Flatid bug feeding on tree sap; occasional visitor to container orchard saplings.
mappings.known_limitations: Sporadic ornamental feeder.

mappings.rationale: Mango leaf-cutting weevil that severs fresh tender mango flushes; specific to orchard mango canopies.
mappings.known_limitations: Attacks only new mango flushes in open orchards.

mappings.rationale: Mango shoot borer moth whose larvae tunnel into young mango growing tips.
mappings.known_limitations: Internal borer restricted to mango shoots.

mappings.rationale: Mango hopper feeding strictly on mango inflorescences causing blossom drop in mature orchard trees.
mappings.known_limitations: Inflorescence specialist of orchard mango trees.

mappings.rationale: Mango branch borer; large cerambycid beetle tunneling inside thick timber branches.
mappings.known_limitations: Timber borer; absent from container gardens.

mappings.rationale: Mango pulp weevil whose grubs feed inside commercial mango fruit pulp.
mappings.known_limitations: Fruit-internal curculionid.

mappings.rationale: Leafhoppers broadly are common foliage pests of terrace container plants, causing stippling, marginal yellowing, and vectoring phytoplasma pathogens.
mappings.known_limitations: Broad family level classification encompassing multiple hopper genera.
